patch_description:
The current program suffers from over-aggressive parameter sharing in Layer 1, where all 9 RY gates share a single parameter "ry_pre" and all 9 RZ gates share "rz_pre". This severely limits the model's ability to learn diverse input encodings. Prior successful programs (score 0.60) used individual RY parameters per qubit, achieving better accuracy.

Additionally, the circuit has three separate shared RZ layers (pre, mid, post), which is redundant. The current design trades expressivity for parameter efficiency but ends up with worse performance.

This edit:
1. Restores individual RY parameters for each qubit (like prior programs) to improve input encoding expressivity
2. Removes the redundant "rz_mid" layer to reduce circuit depth and gate count
3. Replaces the CZ gate at [2,6] with CNOT as suggested in the recommendation to test asymmetric two-qubit coupling
4. Keeps the three-qubit interactions (ZZZ and CCRZ) which provide expressivity

This should improve validation accuracy and reduce the train-test gap while maintaining reasonable parameter efficiency.
